Hi Claire / Samir — great to hear from you. Happy to run a short workshop; below is a compact summary and an initial proposal so you can see the tradeoffs. I'll attach the package matrix and a short "downgrade playbook" for concrete examples.

High-level transition patterns (examples):

- Lift & Pin (fast upgrade):
  * When you upgrade, billing is prorated to the day. Remaining commit is adjusted and can be credited toward the new commitment. We typically offer a one-time migration credit (applied to the first invoice) for pilots moving to a 12+ month reserved commit.
  * Example: if you upgrade on day 45 of a 90-day cycle, you pay pro-rated delta for the remainder; existing unused committed throughput is credited at list-rate toward the new commit.

- Smooth-step downgrade (controlled rollback):
  * Downgrades trigger a 30-day notice by default. "Protected features" (security audits, data retention beyond default, SSO) can be retained for a bounded period using feature-holdback tokens (time-limited), or converted to an add-on SKU.
  * Example: If you lock in Priority Support as part of a pilot and later downgrade, we can keep Priority Support for 60 days as a grace window while you migrate workflows, or convert to a paid add-on at the lower tier.

- Hybrid guardrail (recommended for pilots):
  * For pilots with critical feature dependencies, we recommend a hybrid: upgrade path with an initial migration credit + a 90-day protected-features grace to avoid operational churn. This reduces risk and buys time for your SREs.

Pricing & discount mechanics (pilot-friendly):
- Migration credit: one-time credit up to 10% of remaining commit (negotiable for strategic pilots).
- Ramp discount: if you commit to an annual pilot with a 3-month staged ramp, we can offer a time-limited discount (e.g., 15% first 3 months) to offset integration costs.
- Add-on conversion: protected features can be turned into permanent add-ons at a pre-agreed rate if you downgrade.

Attachments included with this email: package-matrix-v2.pdf (compact matrix), downgrade-playbook.md (step examples), medfolio-mop-plan-sketch.xlsx (sample numbers).

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick 45m workshop — range Tue/Wed next week (I can coordinate with Ben and Lauren for discount approvals).
2) We'll bring a one-page comparison table (Compact vs Throughput vs Dedicated capacities) and 2 simple proration worked examples for your Procurement team.

If that works I'll propose times.

Thanks — Mina

Hi all — quick internal note and decision summary, copying back out so Claire / Samir have the authorized position from Sales ops.

Internal decision (approved):
- Migration credit: approve up to 10% of remaining commit for the pilot (MED-4832), applied as a one-time invoice credit after upgrade.
- Protected-features grace: 60 days standard; extendable to 90 days for the pilot if Medfolio signs the annual pilot by the end of June.
- Ramp discount: approve 15% discount on billable usage for first 3 months of an annual pilot (not combinable with other promotional credits).

Operational notes:
- Downgrade path will include an itemized add-on price list for retention and Priority Support. Legal will include a clause that allows feature holdbacks for migration (explicit end-date).
- Finance asks that any credit be capped and tracked to the deal id (MED-4832) and require a signed SOW pre-commit.
